title: Everybody Was Invited (Mini Movie)
desc: Sienna throws a secret Halloween party while her parents are away — and it gets out of hand.

title: The Thing in the Dark
desc: Ethan sneaks out on Friday night to a horror movie — and has to face what he chose.

title: The Replacement
desc: Maya feels replaced when her best friend Jasmine befriends new girl Sophia.

title: Just One More Chance
desc: Avery learns what forgiveness really means when her best friend keeps asking for just one more chance.

title: The Empty Chair
desc: Jordan has worked hard for the Student Achievement Evening, and Dad has promised to be there — but he has promised before.

title: Between Two Homes
desc: Jordan lives between two homes after the divorce — and the school showcase forces both parents into the same room.

title: Not Your Secret
desc: Sienna's brother Adrian trusts her with a frightening secret — and keeping it could put him in danger.

title: What's Playing?
desc: Amara's little sister has memorized her whole playlist — including a line about getting everything you want no matter who gets hurt.

title: Just Between Us
desc: A private picture Destiny shared with Jace starts circulating among his friends — and she has to decide who she can trust.

title: When Heaven Is Quiet
desc: Gloria has prayed for her little brother Micah's heart condition for six months — and nothing has changed.

title: The Screenshot
desc: Kiara has to decide what loyalty really means when a private screenshot of her friend Nia spreads through school.

title: The Game He Couldn't Play
desc: Mateo has earned the starting point guard spot for the championship final — but the game is Saturday morning, during the Sabbath his family observes.

title: When No One Is Watching
desc: Lena Torres has to decide what honesty is worth when her best friend sends her a leaked copy of the chemistry final.

title: You're Not Invited
desc: Brielle Foster is sure her four closest friends are her whole world — until a Friday-night sleepover happens without her, and she finds out from an Instagram story, not an invitation.

title: God Told Me You're The One
desc: Kellan Brooks is dating Paisley Morgan, who is convinced God told her Kellan is her future husband — and she starts using 'God told me' to keep him from talking to other girls.

title: Not Pretty Enough
desc: Serena Walsh, 17, spends hours scrolling TikTok comparing herself to the girls on her feed — and to her confident best friend Violet Hayes, whose photos always look perfect.

title: Beyond the Screen
desc: Iris Bell, 16, starts watching the fantasy anime Crown of Hollow Moons to fit in with her animation club, but its demonic themes and sexualised fan service leave her uneasy. When her friend Noelle speaks up, Iris pushes her away — and must decide what to keep feeding her mind, and what her friendship is worth.

title: The Perfect Picture
desc: Amara measures herself against the perfect pictures on her phone — and learns where her worth really comes from.

title: The Empty Pew
desc: Sanaa sits alone in the same pew every Sabbath and wonders if anyone notices she is there.

title: Where Do I Belong?
desc: Kenzie Bell hides the faith that matters most to her at school — and feels never quite Christian enough at church — until she has to decide which version of herself she is willing to be.

title: The Pastor's Favourite
desc: Zariah Bennett is the pastor's daughter, the example for every young person in the church — but behind the perfect image she is exhausted by everyone's expectations.

title: Sabbath Double Life
desc: Malachi Bennett keeps noticing the same thing: his youth group friends sing and pray together on Sabbath, then spend the week mocking the very faith they talked about on Saturday.

title: I Don't Feel Forgiven
desc: Nate Brooks told Evan about Zariah's private academic struggles after promising he wouldn't — and four months later he still can't believe God has forgiven him.

title: Man Up
desc: Niran 'Nin' Srisai is still grieving his older brother Kiet, four months after losing him — and everyone around him keeps telling him to man up.

title: The Rumour Wasn't True
desc: Noelle Park is used to eating lunch alone — until a false rumour spreads through Westbrook Secondary and even the truth seems out of reach.

title: Boys Will Be Boys
desc: Darius Cole thinks being funny and confident is all it takes to belong, until Margot calls out the way the boys talk about girls.

title: The Face in the Mirror
desc: Sienna Clarke, 17, a student photographer in Toronto, cannot stop zooming in on her own face — and the more she compares herself to the faces on her screen, the more convinced she becomes that one small change would fix everything. When a school photography project and a quiet conversation with her guidance counsellor, Mrs. Okafor, start asking harder questions, Sienna has to decide what she really believes about beauty, worth, and the girl in the mirror.

title: The Road Ahead
desc: Seventeen-year-old Zara Beckford is in Grade 12, and while her friends celebrate university acceptances, she is still staring at a blank application, feeling like the only one without a plan. With her best friend Aisha already accepted into nursing and her classmate Dante heading into engineering, Zara starts measuring herself against everyone else and wondering if she is falling behind. Conversations with her guidance counsellor, her art teacher, her parents, and her best friend help her untangle what she actually loves — art and design — from what other people expect her to choose. Ellie Grant and Marcus Lee reflect on Jeremiah 29:11, Psalm 32:8, and Proverbs 3:5-6, and on trusting God with the next step even when the whole road is not clear yet.

title: The Open Door
desc: Willa Hartwell notices that new student Kaspar Linden always eats lunch alone, and when she learns he is staying in temporary accommodation, she wants to help. But her first attempts to help — offered in front of everyone, without asking — only embarrass him. With advice from her mother and her youth pastor, Willa learns that real kindness starts by listening and respecting a person's dignity instead of making assumptions. This episode follows Willa as she tries again, quietly and carefully, to offer Kaspar a place to belong. Based on Matthew 25, it is a story about noticing the people others overlook and opening a door — gently.

title: The Words Between Us
desc: Talia Mercer, 16, wears hearing aids — and has become very good at pretending she hears everything. When a misunderstanding at lunch leaves her best friend Harper believing Talia ignored something important, Talia has to decide whether to keep smiling through the gaps or finally explain what she needs. A story about hearing loss, friendship, and learning to ask for room to belong, set in Ottawa.

title: Ready to Say Yes
desc: Juniper Hale is sixteen and has been thinking about baptism for a while, but she isn't sure she's ready. Standing by the baptistry after church one Sunday, she wonders whether she's good enough, what people will think, and whether she's waiting for a feeling that may never come. Over the week she talks honestly with her mum, her best friend Noor, and Pastor Daniel, learning that baptism is about trusting Jesus rather than being perfect. This episode follows Juniper as she asks her questions out loud, prays through her doubts, and works out what it really means to follow Jesus publicly.

title: Slow to Anger
desc: Holly Voss is sixteen and has a quick temper — when something frustrates her, her words come out sharper than she means. After an ordinary family argument leaves her younger brother Felix hurt, Holly starts to notice the same pattern everywhere: snapping at her best friend Maren at school, and answering before she has time to think. With quiet help from her teacher Ms. Vale, her mum, and Pastor Elias, she begins to practise something simple and hard: pausing, breathing, and listening before she responds. This episode follows Holly as she faces what her anger has cost the people she loves, and learns that self-control is not pretending she never feels frustrated — it is choosing what to do with those feelings. A story about words, apologies, and the strength it takes to change one response at a time.

title: A Seat at the Table
desc: Amara Whitaker, 16, has become very good at pretending everything is fine — but when her church youth group plans a community meal, the sign-up sheet says everyone must bring food or contribute ten dollars, and her family can’t spare it. She doesn’t want charity, and she doesn’t want to explain herself; she just wants to belong without having to prove she deserves a seat. With help from her little sister Nia, her friend Jocelyn, and a youth leader willing to listen, Amara challenges the assumption that everyone can give the same thing. A story about financial pressure, dignity, generosity, and what it really means to make room for everyone, with Ellie Grant and Marcus Lee reflecting on James 2:1-4 and 2:15-16.

title: Still My Grandma
desc: Sixteen-year-old Mireya Avelar loves her grandmother Odette, but lately the seventy-eight-year-old has started forgetting things — repeating the same questions, misplacing the things she loves, and sometimes not recognising the people closest to her. Mireya wants to be patient, but the same question for the fifth time in one morning tests her in ways she never expected. With her mother Lucinda's steady wisdom, Mireya begins to learn what it means to honour someone whose memory is slipping, one gentle answer at a time. Join Ellie Grant and Marcus Lee for a warm, honest story about patience, dignity, and loving the people who raised us — even when they start to forget.

title: Clocked In
desc: Sixteen-year-old Emma Tremblay's first part-time job at a Montreal café turns complicated when she discovers her manager isn't paying her for the closing hours she works. With her friend Nadia, her mum, and her coworker Gabriel, Emma keeps careful records and finds the courage to ask for fair pay. A story about honest work and standing up for others.

title: Miles Apart, Still Friends
desc: Sixteen-year-old Wren Calloway's world turns upside down when her best friend Sadie Marlowe tells her the family is moving to another city in just two weeks. As the two girls count down their last days together, Wren tries to freeze everything exactly as it is — while Sadie reaches for a plan to keep their friendship alive across the distance. When silence and hurt feelings start to grow between them, both girls must learn what it means to be honest, to forgive, and to let a friendship change shape without letting it die. (Ecclesiastes 3:1, Proverbs 17:17, Philippians 1:3-6 paraphrased only in the Closing reflection.)

title: The Echo We Leave
desc: Sloane Hayes, 17, is the girl everyone at Edmonton Collegiate is a little afraid of — quick with a joke at someone else's expense, always with her friends Zoe and Kendra laughing along. When her target becomes June Ellis, a quiet photographer who keeps to herself, a hallway joke and a clip filmed on a phone turn into something that follows June everywhere, at school and online. As the laughter spreads, Sloane starts to see what her words actually cost the people around her — and what it feels like when the joke turns back on her. With her teacher Mr. Cole and her mother Tessa each pressing her to look honestly at herself, Sloane has to decide what kind of person she wants to be. Ellie and Marcus close with Matthew 7:12 — treat others the way you want to be treated.

title: The Song Behind the Door
desc: Maren Reid, 16, is a gifted pianist in Saskatoon who only plays when nobody is listening — until her friend Owen overhears her in the church music room and tells everyone. When Maren is asked to play at the church community evening, the fear that has kept her music behind a closed door comes rushing back: what if she makes a mistake, what if people don't like it? As Owen and the people around her keep nudging her toward the piano, Maren has to decide whether hiding her gift is really protecting it — or keeping it from the people it could bless. Ellie and Marcus close with a reminder that your worth isn't measured by how well you perform.

title: When Attention Isn't Love
desc: Nadia Campbell, 16, is single while her friends Tanya and Renee are all getting boyfriends and sharing romantic firsts — and she feels left out. At church, Pastor Daniel talks about relationships, but Nadia barely hears it: all she wants is a boyfriend. She starts changing how she presents herself to get noticed, and her friends get worried. Then the first boy who gives her attention, Dwayne — much older than her — turns out to want her for the wrong reasons. A story about wanting to be wanted, knowing the difference between attention and love, and the friend who notices the real you.

title: The Name on the Box
desc: Micah Hawthorne, 16, volunteers at the community food pantry in Fredericton — until the Thursday package arrives with a name he recognizes: his classmate Ezra Beaumont. Suddenly the boy he sits beside in chemistry is someone whose family needs help, and Micah has to decide what to do with what he knows — protect Ezra's privacy, help quietly, or say something. With his friend Naomi and the pantry coordinator Mara each showing him a different side of kindness, Micah learns that generosity is about how you give, not just what you give. Ellie and Marcus close with Matthew 6:3–4 — give quietly, and let dignity lead.

title: Room for One More
desc: Griffin Ashford, 16, has always had his room to himself — until his family takes in Silas Rowan, a foster teen his own age. Suddenly Griffin's desk, his closet, and his routines all have to stretch to fit someone else, and sharing a room turns out to be about a lot more than clearing a shelf. At school Griffin keeps Silas a secret from his friends, while at home the two boys keep bumping into each other's habits, hurts, and unspoken rules. As jealousy and awkwardness build, both of them have to figure out what it really means to belong somewhere — and whether making room for someone means losing your own place. Ellie and Marcus close with Romans 15, about receiving one another the way Christ has received us.
